ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is product concentration, and the horizontal axis is reaction time; group A corresponds to the 20°C curve, group B corresponds to the 40°C curve, and group C corresponds to the 60°C curve. Before t1, the rising slope of the 40°C curve is obviously greater than that of the 20°C curve, indicating that the product formation rate at 40°C is faster than at 20°C. Reasoning: The other conditions in the question are the same. If the temperature of group A is increased by 10°C from 20°C, it becomes 30°C. In the figure, from 20°C to 40°C, temperature increase is shown to make the enzyme-catalyzed reaction rate increase, and 30°C is still between 20°C and 40°C; therefore, before t1, the rate of the enzyme-catalyzed reaction in group A will speed up.
